questions.q: Cumene is oxidised by air and the product is then treated with dilute acid. The products are:
questions.explain: Air gives cumene hydroperoxide, which dilute acid rearranges and splits into phenol and acetone. Acetophenone forms only as a minor by-product.

questions.q: In the acid-catalysed cleavage of cumene hydroperoxide, which group migrates, and to which atom?
options: Phenyl, from carbon to the electron-deficient oxygen
Methyl, from carbon to the electron-deficient oxygen
Phenyl, from carbon to an adjacent carbocation
questions.explain: As water leaves the protonated –OOH, the oxygen becomes electron-deficient and phenyl, with its higher migratory aptitude, shifts to it. The two methyl groups stay on carbon and end up in acetone.

questions.q: 1,4-Diisopropylbenzene is subjected to the cumene process (air oxidation of both side chains, then dilute acid). The aromatic product is:
questions.explain: Both isopropyl groups become hydroperoxides and each cleaves to an –OH, giving hydroquinone and two molecules of acetone. The 1,3-isomer would give resorcinol.

questions.q: Cyclohexylbenzene hydroperoxide (the –OOH on the ring carbon bearing phenyl) is treated with dilute acid. Using the migration rule of the cumene process, the products are:
questions.explain: Phenyl migrates to oxygen and becomes phenol; the carbon that lost it becomes a C=O, which here is part of the ring, so cyclohexanone forms instead of acetone.
